purpose: Test whether the Technical Operations & Implementation page makes Jamie a truthful, credible, and quickly understandable candidate for public-sector technical operations, product operations, implementation, and delivery roles.

pageBrief.audience: A rushed hiring reader considering Jamie for technical project management, product operations, implementation, civic technology, or adjacent public-interest work.
pageBrief.readerJob: Understand Jamie's operating practice, see three credible situation-to-result chains, find broader capability evidence, and choose a useful hiring action in ninety seconds.
requiredIdeas: Jamie creates operating structure that helps complex public-facing technical work move from ambiguity to launch and handoff.
Three foregrounded situations show sustained business implementation, coalition operating memory, and resident-facing civic product work.
A concise operating method and capability index make the practice transferable without repeating every project narrative.
Collective work remains collectively credited and modeled page-owner review remains distinct from real participation or endorsement.

allowedInputs: the exact rendered public page beginning at /work/technical-operations
public pages reached by following links from that page
the page brief in this contract
the assigned owner's listed public sources
execution.disclaimer: Fictionalized analytical lenses informed by public work. These are not quotations, participation claims, approvals, endorsements, or predictions by the real people named.

owners.name: Jennifer Pahlka
owners.task: Evaluate only whether the page connects Jamie's operational mechanisms to credible institutional or user-facing results while keeping role, collaborators, authority, and causality legible.
owners.criterion: Each foregrounded situation identifies the need, Jamie's responsibility, and what became usable; results are concrete enough to support hiring judgment; collective or institutional outcomes retain careful credit; and the page ends in a useful hiring action.

definitions.pass: A hiring reader can cite three distinct delivery situations, explain Jamie's responsibility in each, and connect the operating work to credible business, coalition, or resident-facing value without inferring solo causality.
definitions.fail: The page lists process without consequences, claims outcomes without responsibility boundaries, confuses artifacts with adoption, or leaves the hiring action unclear.

developmentExamples.label: clear-pass
developmentExamples.inputSummary: Three situation-to-result chains show Jamie's responsibility, careful collective credit, and a relevant hiring next step.

developmentExamples.label: clear-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The page lists project-management activities but gives no delivered or public-facing consequence.

developmentExamples.label: borderline-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: Results are visible, but the reader cannot tell what Jamie did or mistakes a coalition outcome for Jamie's sole achievement.

owners.name: Marianne Bellotti
owners.task: Evaluate only whether the page shows credible implementation work in real systems through concrete mechanisms, constraints, stewardship, learning, and handoff.
owners.criterion: The page names how Jamie frames work, makes ownership and risk visible, coordinates delivery, supports adoption, and leaves maintainable handoffs; the three situations show different operating conditions; and it never treats a document, website, or launch as proof of impact by itself.

definitions.pass: A technical leader can see a repeatable operating practice grounded in sustained implementation, constraints, public boundaries, and specific project evidence.
definitions.fail: The page relies on generic project-management language, presents artifacts as outcomes, omits maintenance or handoff, or hides the constraints that make implementation credible.

developmentExamples.label: clear-pass
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The page connects concrete operating mechanisms to three materially different systems and names adoption and handoff explicitly.

developmentExamples.label: clear-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The page promises cross-functional leadership but shows no mechanism, constraint, maintained system, or handoff.

developmentExamples.label: borderline-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: Project artifacts are specific, but the operating sequence and post-launch stewardship remain invisible.

owners.name: Abby Covert
owners.task: Evaluate only whether the page arranges role, situations, method, capability evidence, and next actions into a coherent mental model for a first-time reader.
owners.criterion: The opening establishes one transferable operating promise; three foregrounded situations carry the main proof; the five-part method explains how Jamie works; the capability section behaves as a compact index rather than a repeated project inventory; and every link has a distinct, understandable destination.

definitions.pass: A first-time reader can explain what Jamie does, remember the three main situations, restate the operating sequence, and use the capability index without constructing the hierarchy themselves.
definitions.fail: The page repeats evidence, presents competing maps, uses insider language, gives equal weight to everything, or makes the reader decide how its parts relate.

developmentExamples.label: clear-pass
developmentExamples.inputSummary: Three stories lead, one five-part method follows, and a compact capability index routes to deeper evidence.

developmentExamples.label: clear-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: Seven promises, eight project summaries, and four proof grids repeat one another without a governing structure.

developmentExamples.label: borderline-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: All content is relevant, but the capability map repeats the foregrounded stories at full length.

owners.name: Deborah Treisman
owners.task: Evaluate only whether the page selects and orders its material into a compact, memorable hiring argument rather than an exhaustive inventory.
owners.criterion: The page progresses from promise to three unequal but complementary situations, then method, supporting evidence, and contact; every section advances the argument; the strongest material receives the most space; and caveats remain proportionate to the accomplishments.

definitions.pass: A rushed reader can follow and remember the argument because selection, sequence, and proportion distinguish the main story from supporting evidence.
definitions.fail: The page restates its thesis, gives equal weight to unequal material, lets protective language overpower accomplishment, or makes the reader find the story inside an inventory.

developmentExamples.label: clear-pass
developmentExamples.inputSummary: Three complementary situations carry the narrative; method and broader proof arrive in supporting roles; the ending converts interest into action.

developmentExamples.label: clear-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: Every project and capability gets a same-size card, so no memorable argument emerges.

developmentExamples.label: borderline-fail
developmentExamples.inputSummary: The story sequence is sound, but repetitive qualifications and duplicated project summaries dilute the strongest accomplishments.

outputSchema.critique: A concrete assessment citing visible rendered-page evidence.
outputSchema.recommendedRevision: The smallest useful change, or No revision needed.
